main_text.head: CAP. IX. Secundum nostrum Argumentum ex Patribus adversus Meritum de Condigno, ex parte Operis boni, ut est Deo debitum.
Argumentatio.
SECT. I.
main_text.p: NUllum opus bonum Morale proprie Deo, ex præcepto, debitum, potest esse de Condigno Meritorium apud Deum: Sed omne opus bonum Morale est proprie Deo, ex præcepto, debitum: Propterea nullum opus bonum Morale potest esse proprie de Condign[?] Meritorium apud Deum.
De Assumptione nulla lis erit. Probanda est Major: primò ex Scripturis.
main_text.head: SECT. II.
main_text.p: LUc. 17. 10. ait Christus Discipulis suis, Cùm omnia feceritis, quæ præcepta sunt vo-bis, dicite, Servi inutiles sumus; quod debuimus facere, fecimus. Quæ verba nobis videntur omnem Meriti bonorum operum opinionem labefactare

page.notes: The initial N and L are decorated woodcut initials, joined to the following word. A dark blot covers the last letter of "Condigno" in the paragraph of SECT. I; the reading "Condign[?]" is uncertain. The final word "labefactare" stands on its own short line at the right; it completes the sentence and is read as text, not as a catchword, although it could be a catchword. No catchword or signature is clearly printed. The heading levels for SECT. and Probatio are a judgement from their size and placement.
